title: Present perfect continuous
note: have/has been + -ing. The Czech trap is the PRESENT tense: Učím se anglicky pět let -> *I learn / *I am learning English for five years. Recycles for/since from a2_for_since (same job, no re-teach). Contrast card + sort drills how many (simple) vs how long (continuous) - B12, because Czech cannot pick that one. State verbs (know / have = own / be / like) take no -ing and have their own card, so the Quiz distractor *have been knowing* is taught first (C11). Use is error-correction (E7). First draft 2026-09-02, core half - thicken after smoke.

table.caption: frame
rows: started before now, still going now

examples.en: I **have been** learning English for five years.
She **has been** working here since March.

points: The action is not over. It began in the past and it is still happening.

cards.title: Czech says it in the present
points: Czech uses the **present tense** for something that started earlier and still goes on. English does not.

rows: I **have been** learning English for five years.
We **have been** waiting for an hour.
It **has been** snowing since this morning.

cards.title: How long? for and since

rows: **for** five years · **for** an hour · **for** two days

examples.en: They **have been** living in Brno **since** last year.
I **have been** waiting for twenty minutes.

points: You already know **for** and **since** from the present perfect. They do the same job here.

cards.title: Questions and negatives

rows: He **hasn't been** feeling well since Monday.

points: In a question the subject goes **between** have and been.

cards.title: How many, or how long?

rows: I **have read** three books this month.
how long — she may still be writing

points: Count the things → the simple. Measure the time → the continuous.

cards.title: Verbs that take no -ing

rows: I **have known** her for ten years.
He **has been** ill for a week.
I **have liked** it since I was a child.

points: These verbs describe a **state**, not an activity. The duration still needs the present perfect — just without **-ing**.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: The Czech present tense is the trap. Say **have been** + **-ing**.

rows: I **have been** learning English for five years.
~~I am learning English for five years.~~
I **have been** learning English for five years.
~~I have been knowing her for ten years.~~
I **have known** her for ten years.
She **has been** working here since March.

items.en: I have been learning English for five years.
accepts: I have been learning English for five years.
I've been learning English for five years.
items.wrong: I learn English for five years.
items.explanation: Czech uses the present here. English needs **have been** + **-ing** — it started five years ago and is still going.
items.explanation_cz: Čeština má přítomný čas. Angličtina potřebuje **have been + -ing** — začalo to před pěti lety a pořád to trvá.

items.en: She has been working here since March.
accepts: She has been working here since March.
She's been working here since March.
items.explanation: **since** + a point in time (March). Third person takes **has** been working.
items.explanation_cz: **since** + bod v čase (March). Ve třetí osobě **has** been working.

items.en: We have been waiting for an hour.
accepts: We have been waiting for an hour.
We've been waiting for an hour.
items.wrong: We are waiting for an hour.
items.explanation: **for** + a length of time. The waiting started an hour ago and has not stopped.
items.explanation_cz: **for** + délka času. Čekání začalo před hodinou a ještě neskončilo.

items.en: They have been living in Brno since last year.
items.gap: They ____ in Brno since last year. (live)
accepts: They have been living in Brno since last year.
They've been living in Brno since last year.
items.wrong: They live in Brno since last year.
items.explanation: **since last year** — it began then and they are still there. **have been living**.
items.explanation_cz: **since last year** — začalo to tehdy a pořád tam bydlí. **have been living**.

items.en: How long have you been waiting?
accepts: How long have you been waiting?
items.explanation: Question order: **have** + you + **been** + waiting. The subject sits between **have** and **been**.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **have** + you + **been** + waiting. Podmět je mezi **have** a **been**.

items.en: How long has it been raining?
accepts: How long has it been raining?
items.explanation: **it** is third person, so **has** it been raining. Not *is it raining* — that asks about right now only.
items.explanation_cz: **it** je třetí osoba, tedy **has** it been raining. Ne *is it raining* — to se ptá jen na tuto chvíli.

items.en: I haven't been sleeping well.
accepts: I haven't been sleeping well.
I have not been sleeping well.
items.explanation: Negative: **haven't been** + sleeping. The bad sleep started earlier and is still going.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor: **haven't been** + sleeping. Špatné spaní začalo dřív a pořád trvá.

items.en: He hasn't been feeling well since Monday.
accepts: He hasn't been feeling well since Monday.
He has not been feeling well since Monday.
items.wrong: He doesn't feel well since Monday.
items.explanation: Third person negative: **hasn't been** feeling. **since Monday** marks where it started.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor ve třetí osobě: **hasn't been** feeling. **since Monday** říká, odkdy.

items.en: I have read three books this month.
items.cz: Tento měsíc jsem přečetl tři knihy.
accepts: I have read three books this month.
I've read three books this month.
items.explanation: **Three books** is how many — a finished result. Use the simple: **have read**.
items.explanation_cz: **Tři knihy** je kolik — hotový výsledek. Použij prostý tvar: **have read**.

items.en: I have been reading all afternoon.
accepts: I have been reading all afternoon.
I've been reading all afternoon.
items.explanation: **All afternoon** is how long, not how many. Use **have been reading**.
items.explanation_cz: **Celé odpoledne** je jak dlouho, ne kolik. Použij **have been reading**.

items.en: I have known her for ten years.
accepts: I have known her for ten years.
I've known her for ten years.
items.wrong: I have been knowing her for ten years.
items.explanation: **know** is a state, so no **-ing**. The duration still needs the present perfect: **have known**.
items.explanation_cz: **know** je stav, takže žádné **-ing**. Délku času ale pořád nese předpřítomný čas: **have known**.

items.en: We have had this car since 2019.
accepts: We have had this car since 2019.
We've had this car since 2019.
items.wrong: We have been having this car since 2019.
items.explanation: **have** here means own — a state, so no **-ing**. **have had** + since.
items.explanation_cz: **have** tu znamená vlastnit — je to stav, takže žádné **-ing**. **have had** + since.

items.en: I am tired. I have been looking at a screen all day.
items.cz: Jsem unavený. Celý den koukám na obrazovku.
items.gap: I ____ at a screen all day. (look)
accepts: I am tired. I have been looking at a screen all day.
I'm tired. I've been looking at a screen all day.
I am tired. I've been looking at a screen all day.
I'm tired. I have been looking at a screen all day.
items.explanation: The tiredness now comes from an activity that has run **all day**: **have been** looking.
items.explanation_cz: Únava teď je z činnosti, která běží **celý den**: **have been** looking.

items.en: It has been snowing since this morning.
accepts: It has been snowing since this morning.
It's been snowing since this morning.
items.explanation: **since this morning** — it started then and it is still snowing. **has been snowing**.
items.explanation_cz: **since this morning** — začalo to ráno a pořád sněží. **has been snowing**.

items.en: I have **been waiting** for an hour.
She has **been working** here since March.
It has **been raining** all day.
They have **been living** here since 2019.
I **have read** three books this month.
She **has written** two emails.
We **have finished** the work.
I **have seen** that film twice.
